paper.title: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
paper.central_claim: Interactive agent-human tasks (structured instructions) identify privacy-sensitive pages and align with personalised needs, and integrating Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) information in the model's in-context input yields state-of-the-art action success among LLMs on AitW (overall 66.92%) without extra inference cost.

evidence.quote: achieves state-of-the-art performance in LLMs without incurring additional inference costs
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim 1 (SOTA among LLMs, no extra inference cost).

evidence.quote: boasting an overall action success rate of 66.92%
evidence.support_explanation: Headline number; metric is the offline task-completion score.

evidence.quote: SOPs abstract and generalize operational instructions, eschewing the specification of explicit operation types.
evidence.support_explanation: SOP = abstract subtask pipeline.

evidence.quote: We also integrate the current status of task execution into the SOPs, enabling the model to more effectively understand past actions and anticipate future tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: SOP carries per-subtask completion state and outlines future subtasks.

evidence.quote: This implies that the uncertainty of Y Y , given both X X and Z Z , is potentially reduced compared to when only X X is known.
evidence.support_explanation: Entropy argument: H(Y|X,Z)<=H(Y|X) holds for any Z, so it does not distinguish a useful SOP from a leaked one.

evidence.quote: into the in-context input and mixed it with the original samples
evidence.support_explanation: SOP samples are MIXED with original samples in training (extra data exposure vs plain Llama 2 not controlled).

evidence.quote: During the prediction phase, this approach allows consistency with the original prompt, eliminating the need for additional tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Ambiguous: could mean the inference prompt has no SOP (training-time augmentation) or that no extra pass is needed; text never states how SOP is obtained at test time.

evidence.quote: For offline training, we utilize a combination of samples, ensuring that this approach incurs no additional costs in practical usage.
evidence.support_explanation: Suggests SOP is an offline-training device; conflicts with Sec 4.2 'SOP ... outline subsequent actions' and Table 3 prompt containing SOP.

evidence.quote: The Llama 2+SOP approach involves adding key abstract subtask pipelines to the input prompt while also marking the completion status of each subtask in the current process.
evidence.support_explanation: Llama 2+SOP input includes the full subtask pipeline with finish/unfinish states (Table 3 shows the complete pipeline including future subtasks).

evidence.quote: SOP encapsulate historical operational behaviors and outline subsequent actions
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' own explanation says SOP outlines subsequent actions, i.e. contains future information.

evidence.quote: we trained a BERT-based classification model

signatures.object: action-prediction prompt of a LoRA-fine-tuned LLM (Llama 2 on AitW; Qwen-7B in AIA)
signatures.information: task goal, role text, previous actions, current-screen element list (OCR/icon-detected text/type), plus SOP: abstract subtask pipeline with per-subtask finish/unfinish state. SOP derivation: AitW = hand-designed click-text/icon -> subtask mapping (Table 7, negative actions removed, similar subtasks merged); AIA = BERT classifier over click text into 13 subtasks. Source of SOP at inference NOT stated.
signatures.operation: SFT on a mixture of SOP-augmented and original samples; compare against output-side plan and plan+state under identical training recipe (5 epochs, lr 5e-5, 8xA100)
signatures.output: action type + element (id) / text; swipe as direction
signatures.conditions: needs a subtask vocabulary and completion tracking per episode; instruction-level pipeline variability (29 per instruction)
signatures.feedback: none at inference beyond history; SOP states are label-derived
signatures.selection_rule: negative actions and 'Others' clicks excluded from SOP; classifier decides sub-task
signatures.selection_data: same demonstrations used for SFT (episode-wise split)
signatures.persistence: SOP is data in training samples; test-time storage/retrieval not described
signatures.failure_boundary: plan-in-output hurts; GPT-4V higher on Single; no unseen-app/instruction test; test-time SOP leakage not ruled out

signatures.information: element boxes of the screen; click coordinates
signatures.operation: expand each element's box so click coordinates map uniquely to an element; train the model to output the element (id/text/type) rather than coordinates; swipe -> direction with fixed distance
signatures.conditions: screen yields element list with boxes
signatures.claimed_effect: none isolated (no ablation vs coordinate output)
signatures.failure_boundary: cannot target sub-element positions; ICL baselines under different protocols

signatures.object: Structured Instruction output for user-confirmation pages (AIA)
signatures.information: DOM fragments of the current page
signatures.operation: model emits structured notification text + user options; user chooses, replacing direct model execution

signatures.failure_boundary: no precision/recall of privacy detection, no user study, contractor data

gap.author_gap: (1) agents struggle to relate the current page to the task goal from fragmented, redundant demonstrations; (2) privacy-related decisions need user awareness/confirmation; (3) stronger predictors (planning, chaining, extra small models) cost inference time.
gap.checked_gap: (1) is partially evidenced: 29 pipelines/instruction and plan-in-output lowering Llama 2 by 3.35 points (author-reported, offline). (2) is asserted without any measured incidence, user study, or comparison with a confirmation-handling baseline. (3) is supported by Table 5 (plan variants 5-6x output tokens, 0.117-0.123 s vs 0.071 s).

matches.reason: Closest of the 15 mains: a process specification is supplied as conditioning. claims.text: Llama 2+SOP achieves SOTA among LLMs on AitW with overall 66.92%.
claims.setting: AitW, offline per-episode partial correctness averaged over 5 subsets; LoRA SFT, 5 epochs
claims.selection_vs_test: episode-wise split; shared instructions across splits; GoogleApps 10% sample; SOP test-time source unstated
claims.result_denominator: test episode counts per subset not reported; single run; Overall = mean of 5 subset scores (our check: 66.92 exact)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported: the SOP variant scored 1.49 points above the same-recipe Llama 2 baseline on an offline metric; higher than the plan variants and the listed in-context models; ties/loses to GPT-4V on Single (78.29 vs 76.27). Not shown SOTA against Auto-UI/BC agent (cited, absent). Gain may arise from leakage or extra mixed data.

claims.text: SOP does not increase inference cost.
claims.result_denominator: s per inference, hardware not stated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Output length and measured latency equal the baseline; input prompt length (SOP adds tokens) not reported; if SOP must be produced at test time its production cost is not counted.

claims.text: SOP improves AIA instruction generation (Operational/Task Status/Structured).
claims.setting: private AIA, Qwen-7B LoRA SFT, ~2,000 test episodes
claims.allowed_conclusion: On an unreleased offline test set, SOP-augmented Qwen-7B scored higher on three instruction types; not reproducible, not user-tested.

claims.text: Structured instructions identify sensitive pages and align with personalised needs via human-machine interaction.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A reformatting capability with a 0.606 offline score; privacy identification and personalization are not evaluated.

assessment.evidence_level_note: offline AitW per-episode partial scores and a private offline AIA test set; no online/interactive task success
assessment.author_claim_preserved: Interactive agent-human tasks (structured instructions) identify privacy-sensitive pages and align with personalised needs, and integrating Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) information in the model's in-context input yields state-of-the-art action success among LLMs on AitW (overall 66.92%) without extra inference cost.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: on AitW (offline, single run) a Llama 2 variant trained with SOP-augmented prompts scored 66.92 vs 65.43 for the same-recipe baseline and lower for output-side plan variants; measured decoding latency/outputs equal the baseline. Not reproduced.
assessment.cannot_say: that SOP gives deployable gains without leakage; that the method is SOTA versus Auto-UI/BC agent; that human-machine interaction handles privacy; any online success.
unresolved: how/where SOP is obtained at test time (Fig 2 prompt shows no SOP field; Sec 5 says 'offline training' only; Table 3/Sec 4.2 say SOP in input)
protocol/source of GPT-4V, Palm 2, ChatGPT baseline numbers

retention_trace.reason: static prompted/fine-tuned predictor; SOP is part of training/inference inputs, no select-and-persist loop claimed

G.reason: Real limitations are named (redundant demonstrations, privacy confirmation, inference cost) and (1)/(3) have some evidence, but nearest neighbours that tackle the same bottleneck (Auto-UI, BC agent, plan-based agents) are cited yet not compared; privacy gap has no incidence measurement.

M.reason: Concrete idea (move abstract subtask progress to input instead of output plan) with a checkable prediction (plan hurts, SOP helps, latency unchanged) that Table 4/5 are consistent with; but the entropy argument is vacuous for any Z, and the mechanism depends on an undescribed test-time SOP source; enlarged-element and structured-instruction rationales are thin.

X.reason: SOP vocabulary construction (Table 7, BERT classifier, exclusions) and training mixture are described, but how SOP/finish-state is computed for an unseen test episode is not stated (text contradicts itself between Sec 4.2, Sec 5 and Fig 2); structured-instruction model/labels/training and decision rule undocumented; enlarged-element matching tolerance not specified; proprietary data/code not evaluable here.

E.measurement.reason: Offline per-episode partial score only (E15 unmet); the definition of a correct click under enlarged-element matching and of 'highest' vs GPT-4V rows is unclear; baseline numbers come from unstated protocols; AIA scores are on private contractor-simulated data with no judge/user validation.

E.causality.reason: Same-recipe controls (plan, plan+state) are useful, but SOP training mixes SOP and original samples (extra exposure not controlled), no ablation of enlarged-element or structured instruction, gain +1.49 on a single run, and possible test-time leakage of future subtasks (authors say SOP 'outline subsequent actions') cannot be excluded.

E.holdout.reason: Episode-wise split with shared instructions (avg 29 pipelines per instruction) lets SOP be derived from training episodes of the same instruction; no unseen-app/instruction test; GoogleApps 10% sample; AIA from the same contractor pipeline; 'SOTA' scope exceeds the single dataset.

E.statistics.reason: No seeds, variance or confidence intervals, no per-subset test sizes, differences of 0.5-2.5 points reported as superiority ('highest in all experiments' is contradicted for Single); searched Secs 4.1-4.2, Tables 1-5, Appendix for any variance/significance statement.

E.cost.reason: Decoding latency and output tokens are measured (Table 5, vLLM) and training compute/epochs stated; SOP input length, SOP production cost at test time, and data-exposure differences are not reported; GPT-4V/Palm/ChatGPT rows are not budget-matched.

status_reason: complete text and shared figures read; the SOP test-time source is not stated anywhere in the material (scored as X/E weaknesses, not unknown)
short_reason: Practical-engineering paper: the same-recipe plan/plan+state controls and latency table are useful, but evidence is offline-only, single run, +1.49 points, on a split where instructions repeat, and the paper never states where the SOP comes from at test time (its own explanation says SOP 'outlines subsequent actions'), so leakage or extra-data effects cannot be excluded. Human-machine-interaction claim has only a private offline score.
